cohort: 80 mothers and their term infants, divided into vaginal delivery (n=40) and cesarean section (n=40) groups
finding: Infants born vaginally had higher levels of native-thiol and total-thiol in cord blood and lower levels of disulfide at 24 hours, suggesting less oxidative stress compared to infants born by cesarean.
